items.grounds: Re-derived from bytes both ways. The preceding row's span is Eccl.1.12-Eccl.1.15 and its opening verse begins אֲנִ֣י קֹהֶ֗לֶת הָיִ֥יתִי מֶ֛לֶךְ (oshb:Eccl.1.12, byte tier; the verse's first four tokens); the natan-plus-lev construction וְנָתַ֣תִּי אֶת לִבִּ֗י (oshb:Eccl.1.13, byte tier) stands in that row's SECOND verse, so the shipped clause 'the natan-plus-lev construction that opened the preceding row at 1:13' is false as a claim about the neighbour row, contradicts that row's own account (1:12 restates the royal self-identification; 1:13 'continues into the first wisdom inquiry'), and is a positional row reference the book's register purge bars outright. The recurrence the sentence exists to disclose is TRUE: וָאֶתְּנָ֤ה לִבִּי֙ לָדַ֣עַת (oshb:Eccl.1.17, byte tier) is the same natan-root-plus-lev construction in a different inflected form (the 1:13 form recurs as a contiguous skeleton phrase at 2 verses book-wide, 1:13 and 8:16; the 1:17 form at 1 verse book-wide), so the 'disclosed here rather than implied absent' posture survives and the falsity is confined to the positional attribution. BOTH SIDES of the 1:15|1:16 seam weighed: 1:15 closes on the gnomic couplet וְחֶסְר֖וֹן לֹא יוּכַ֥ל לְהִמָּנֽוֹת (oshb:Eccl.1.15, byte tier) with no hevel refrain, and 1:16 opens on the self-address formula דִּבַּ֨רְתִּי אֲנִ֤י עִם לִבִּי֙ (oshb:Eccl.1.16, byte tier; sweep: 2 verses book-wide carry the dibbarti token, 1:16 and 2:15), the word-bound content-token intersection of 1:15 x 1:16 being empty; the formula onset decides the seam under the book's monologue rule, so the false clause is not load-bearing. Verdict: confirm at medium under the register lane's E-18 arm (a false cross-row claim, not load-bearing; low would understate a byte-false statement about a neighbour row's structure). Repair validated: re-anchoring on the verses alone ('the natan-plus-lev construction standing at 1:13 ... recurs inside this row at 1:17') is byte-sound provided 'recurs' is read as the same construction in different inflected forms rather than a word-bound identity; field repair only, no span effect.

Re-derived from bytes both ways. The rival field concedes the clause break, הִגְדַּ֖לְתִּי מַעֲשָׂ֑י (oshb:Eccl.2.4, byte tier; the verse's asyndetic first tokens), and rejects the split on two objects that both stop short of the contested 2:3|2:4 seam: the word-bound skeleton token li counts 0 at 2:3, then 2/1/1/2/2/1 across 2:4-2:9 and 0 at 2:10 (six verses, matching the row's digit, none of them 2:3), and the contiguous skeleton phrase lifnay-birushalaim returns 2 verses book-wide (2:7, 2:9). The word-bound content-token intersection of 2:3 x 2:4 is EMPTY, so nothing the row cites explains why 2:3 belongs with 2:4-2:10; the warrant offered never reaches the rival it is aimed at. BOTH SIDES of the seam weighed under the book's monologue rule (formula onsets open units): 2:3 closes on its purpose clause מִסְפַּ֖ר יְמֵ֥י חַיֵּיהֶֽם (oshb:Eccl.2.3, byte tier) with no closural refrain, and 2:4 opens on a plain narrative perfect carrying no self-address or turning formula (the tarti frame תַּ֣רְתִּי בְלִבִּ֔י (oshb:Eccl.2.3, byte tier) is unique, sweep: 1 verse book-wide; the turning formula u-faniti returns 2 verses, 2:11 and 2:12; no amarti, dibbarti, shavti or raiti token stands at 2:4), so no ruled onset device opens a unit at 2:4 and the rival fails on bytes the row never states. The outer seams are independently warranted (tarti at 2:3; the turning formula at 2:11), so the defect is a misdirected rival warrant, not load-bearing: confirm at medium. Repair validated with qualification: the experiment-frame ground is byte-sound (2:3's frame verb plus its purpose clause עַ֣ד אֲשֶׁר אֶרְאֶ֗ה אֵי זֶ֨ה ט֜וֹב לִבְנֵ֤י הָאָדָם֙ (oshb:Eccl.2.3, byte tier), which the self-benefit catalogue of 2:4-2:9 executes) and may add the lexeme-level heart and wisdom bracket, וְלִבִּ֞י נֹהֵ֤ג בַּֽחָכְמָה֙ (oshb:Eccl.2.3, byte tier) against כִּֽי לִבִּ֤י שָׂמֵ֨חַ֙ (oshb:Eccl.2.10, byte tier) and אַ֥ף חָכְמָתִ֖י עָ֥מְדָה לִּֽי (oshb:Eccl.2.9, byte tier), but only as root-level texture, never as word-bound identity (the 2:3 x 2:9 and 2:3 x 2:10 word-bound content intersections are also empty). Field repair to strongest_rejected_alternative or boundary_rationale only; no respan.

Re-derived from bytes both ways. The shavti turn stands at 4:7, וְשַׁ֧בְתִּי אֲנִ֛י וָאֶרְאֶ֥ה (oshb:Eccl.4.7, byte tier; sweep: 3 verses book-wide carry the shavti/veshavti token, 4:1, 4:7, 9:11), which establishes the PRECEDING unit's opening at 4:6|4:7, not the 4:8|4:9 seam this row's device_notes assigns to it ('the independent shavti-restart boundary already established at web:Eccl.4.7-Eccl.4.8|Eccl.4.9'); the embedded 4:7-4:8 row likewise argues its opening and 4:8's content but never its close, so the seam is un-argued from both rows. boundary_rationale names no seam device at all (continuity 'answers the solitary toiler of 4:8', the opening quotation, an illustration count and the closing quotation), and the only form evidence (no first-person verb; three distinct lead particles) sits in the unit_type rival. BOTH SIDES of 4:8|4:9 weighed from bytes: 4:8 closes on the verdict refrain גַּם זֶ֥ה הֶ֛בֶל וְעִנְיַ֥ן רָ֖ע הֽוּא (oshb:Eccl.4.8, byte tier; the contiguous skeleton phrase gam-zeh-hevel returns 13 verses book-wide and the appended ve-inyan-ra 1 verse), a refrain close under the book's rule; 4:9 opens on the comparative טוֹבִ֥ים הַשְּׁנַ֖יִם מִן הָאֶחָ֑ד (oshb:Eccl.4.9, byte tier), a genuine tov-min construction whose plural first token and intervening subject keep it out of both the contiguous tov-min adjacency inventory and the tov-opener inventory (sweep: 3 verses book-wide carry the plural tovim, 4:9, 7:10, 11:6, only 4:9 verse-initial; the phrase min-ha-echad 1 verse); the word-bound content-token intersection of 4:8 x 4:9 is empty. Both sides decide the seam independently of the shavti restart, and the row's form claims re-derive true (no first-person -ti form and no ani token in 4:9-4:12; lead particles ki-im, gam-im, ve-im at their own refs). The rear seam also holds: 4:12 closes לֹ֥א בִמְהֵרָ֖ה יִנָּתֵֽק (oshb:Eccl.4.12, byte tier) and 4:13 opens on the inventory tov-opener ט֛וֹב יֶ֥לֶד מִסְכֵּ֖ן וְחָכָ֑ם (oshb:Eccl.4.13, byte tier), intersection empty. The span is unchallenged and the seam byte-sound, so the defect is an absent/misdirected warrant in the driver field: confirm at medium. Repair validated with qualification: restating the seam from 4:8's refrain close and 4:9's comparative onset is byte-sound, but 4:9 must be cited as a construction check with the digits above, not as an inventory site, and the cross-seam ordinal echo ve-ein-sheni (sweep: 2 verses, 4:8 and 4:10) stays disclosed as the row already does. Field repair only; no respan.

Re-derived from bytes with the object named. The row attaches the digit to 'the laughter root' while quoting only the defective spelling: the contiguous skeleton sweep of that spelling returns 2 verses / 2 tokens book-wide, מִשְּׂחֹ֑ק (oshb:Eccl.7.3, byte tier) and שְׂחֹ֣ק (oshb:Eccl.7.6, byte tier); the plene spelling with the mater vav returns 3 further verses / 3 tokens, לִשְׂח֖וֹק (oshb:Eccl.2.2, byte tier), לִשְׂח֔וֹק (oshb:Eccl.3.4, byte tier) and לִשְׂחוֹק֙ (oshb:Eccl.10.19, byte tier); a token-level pass over all 222 MT verses finds no third spelling, so the root the sentence names stands in 5 verses / 5 tokens book-wide, not 2. This is the mater-lectionis hazard of the book's own catalogue (sweep per attested spelling; name spelling versus root before counting): a false digit for the named object. Not load-bearing, re-derived: the mourning word returns 2 verses book-wide (7:2, 7:4), both inside the span; the laughter-envelope rival is rejected on the word-bound content-token intersection of 7:5 x 7:6, which is EMPTY; and the corrected digit only weakens that rival, whose root is not exclusive to 7:3-7:6. BOTH SIDES of the 7:4|7:5 closing seam the envelope would erase: 7:4 closes וְלֵ֥ב כְּסִילִ֖ים בְּבֵ֥ית שִׂמְחָֽה (oshb:Eccl.7.4, byte tier) and 7:5 opens on the inventory tov-opener ט֕וֹב לִשְׁמֹ֖עַ גַּעֲרַ֣ת חָכָ֑ם (oshb:Eccl.7.5, byte tier; 4th of the chapter's 7 tov-opener sites), the formula onset deciding the seam, while the fools word straddling it (word-bound: 7:4, 7:5, 7:9) is disclosed by the row as topic texture. Confirm at medium. Repair validated: either wording proposed is byte-true (defective spelling 2 verses with the plene spelling adding 3 further verses, or the root at 5 verses book-wide); field repair only, no span effect.

Re-derived from bytes. oshb:Eccl.7.14 carries the two runs consecutively, רָעָ֖ה רְאֵ֑ה (oshb:Eccl.7.14, byte tier): the first is the resh-ayin noun in וּבְי֥וֹם רָעָ֖ה (oshb:Eccl.7.14, byte tier; the phrase is unique, sweep: 1 verse book-wide), the second the imperative רְאֵ֑ה גַּ֣ם אֶת זֶ֤ה (oshb:Eccl.7.14, byte tier), the verse's last imperative after הֱיֵ֣ה בְט֔וֹב (oshb:Eccl.7.14, byte tier) and matching the pair's opening imperative רְאֵ֖ה אֶת מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים (oshb:Eccl.7.13, byte tier). device_notes item (1) labels the noun run as the raah root of 7:14's own closing imperative while item (2) of the same field correctly assigns that very run to the resh-ayin root: one byte run, two roots, one field. Byte-valid splice, semantically the wrong word for the claim, a defect regardless of when the ledger named the class. Ruled coherently with the neighbour row at Eccl.7.13-Eccl.7.14, which describes the same seam with the correct token (its closing imperative recurring as the perfect רָאִ֖יתִי (oshb:Eccl.7.15, byte tier)): the two rows must agree and the neighbour is right. BOTH SIDES of the 7:14|7:15 seam weighed: 7:14 closes on the purpose clause שֶׁלֹּ֨א יִמְצָ֧א הָֽאָדָ֛ם אַחֲרָ֖יו מְאֽוּמָה (oshb:Eccl.7.14, byte tier) inside an imperative-register verse, and 7:15 opens on the observation frame אֶת הַכֹּ֥ל רָאִ֖יתִי בִּימֵ֣י הֶבְלִ֑י (oshb:Eccl.7.15, byte tier; the raiti token returns 18 verses book-wide and the inventory lists 7:15), the word-bound content-token intersection of 7:14 x 7:15 being empty; the register shift (imperative to first-person report) decides the seam, exactly as the row independently states, so the mis-splice is texture-level and not load-bearing. Confirm at medium. Repair validated: replacing the splice in item (1) with רְאֵ֑ה (oshb:Eccl.7.14, byte tier) is byte-sound, with the one qualification that 'closing imperative' means the verse's last imperative, not its last word; item (2) already holds the noun under the resh-ayin root and needs no edit. Field repair only; no respan.

Re-derived from bytes. Chapter 7 is identity (crosswalk: WEB 7:19 = MT 7:19, WEB 7:14 = MT 7:14), so web:Eccl.7.19 stands five verses past the ruled sentence zone's close at web:Eccl.7.14, the first verse outside it being web:Eccl.7.15; the row's twice-repeated 'one verse outside' (boundary_rationale and device_notes) is false. The proximity premise fails with it: the verses immediately before 7:19 are the moderation admonition of 7:16-7:18, closing on כִּֽי יְרֵ֥א אֱלֹהִ֖ים יֵצֵ֥א אֶת כֻּלָּֽם (oshb:Eccl.7.18, byte tier), not sentence-zone sayings, and the row's own rival field and device_notes call the verse 'distinct in FORM' from the zone's tov-min sayings, contradicting boundary_rationale's 'of the same form as the sentence-zone sayings just before it' inside one row. BOTH SIDES of each seam weighed: 7:18's second-person prohibition series with its gnomic grounding clause closes against 7:19's third-person maxim onset הַֽחָכְמָ֖ה תָּעֹ֣ז לֶחָכָ֑ם (oshb:Eccl.7.19, byte tier; the verb and the noun of its comparative מֵֽעֲשָׂרָה֙ שַׁלִּיטִ֔ים (oshb:Eccl.7.19, byte tier) each return 1 verse book-wide), and 7:19 closes אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָי֖וּ בָּעִֽיר (oshb:Eccl.7.19, byte tier) against 7:20's fresh maxim onset כִּ֣י אָדָ֔ם אֵ֥ין צַדִּ֖יק בָּאָ֑רֶץ (oshb:Eccl.7.20, byte tier); the word-bound content-token intersections 7:18 x 7:19 and 7:19 x 7:20 are both empty, so both seams rest on the register shifts the row states and neither moves. The false distance is not load-bearing on a seam, and not decisive for the unit_type licence either, since device_notes grounds the deviation on the verse's own construction (a verbal comparative with no observation frame), which re-derives true; it is a false positional digit deployed twice as a premise: confirm at medium. Repair validated with qualification: correct the distance in both fields, re-argue single_saying from the construction alone, and resolve the internal form contradiction in favour of the rival/device_notes reading (distinct in form, same genre), on which the licence actually depends; no driver swap is entailed, so unit_type and confidence re-open only formally and the bytes give no reason to change them. Field repair only; no respan.

Re-derived from bytes with the object named (MT refs; the one offset-zone site written as a dual). Verses carrying the bare word-bound skeleton token ruach: 13 book-wide (1:14, 1:17, 2:11, 2:17, 2:26, 3:21, 4:4, 4:6, 4:16, 6:9, 7:8, 10:4, 11:4), exactly the auditor's list; verses carrying ANY token on that skeleton: 20 book-wide, the staged inventory's own ruach_any object, the 7 additional sites all carrying prefixed, definite or suffixed forms (1:6, 3:19, MT 5:15 = WEB 5:16, 7:9, 8:8, 11:5, 12:7). שֹׁמֵ֥ר ר֖וּחַ לֹ֣א יִזְרָ֑ע (oshb:Eccl.11.4, byte tier) carries the bare form; מַה דֶּ֣רֶךְ הָר֔וּחַ (oshb:Eccl.11.5, byte tier) carries the definite form and no bare token, so device_notes' 'the bare ruach word-bound form occurs at 20 verses book-wide, and these two ch-11 sites carry it' is false twice for the object it names (digit 13, not 20; 11:5 not a site), while observed_substrate_signals' 'any-ruach ... sweep: 20 verses' points at the inventory object and is true. The book's own count-object law (name the object, then count) is breached inside a row that otherwise observes it: a false digit claim that is not load-bearing, since device_notes itself holds the wind vocabulary as 'texture, not a boundary device' and no seam or rival rests on it. both_sides_assessed is false because this is a count-object texture item concerning no seam (the digit touches neither of the row's outer seams and the finding puts none in question). Confirm at medium. Repair validated: either restoration proposed is byte-true (the any-token object at 20 verses, or the bare word-bound object at 13 verses with 11:4 the only ch-11 site and the definite form at 11:5 named separately), with the qualification that the 20-verse object blends the wind, breath, spirit and temper senses (7:9's suffixed form is 'your spirit') and should be cited as the inventory's any-token object without a sense claim. Field repair only; no span effect.
